title: The Roman Emperor Who Declared War On The Ocean
sources: Suetonius, The Lives of the Twelve Caesars (Life of Caligula, ch. 46)

lines.text: In forty AD, Roman Emperor Caligula declared war on the God of the Sea.
lines.caps: In *40 AD, | Rome declared *war | on the *Sea God.

lines.text: Not an invading army. The literal ocean.
He marched two hundred thousand legionaries all the way to France,
ready to cross the stormy English Channel and invade Britain.
But when they reached the shore, Caligula suddenly changed his mind.
lines.caps: But at the *beach, | he *changed his mind.

lines.text: He declared Neptune, the Lord of the Sea, was Rome's mortal enemy.
So he ordered his legions to draw their iron swords,
lines.caps: He ordered his *legions | to draw their *swords,

lines.text: form a battle line on the sand, and viciously stab the waves.
Catapults fired heavy boulders straight into the water.
And when the ocean refused to surrender,
lines.caps: And when the sea | *refused to surrender,

lines.text: he commanded every soldier to fill their helmets with seashells,
declaring them captured spoils of war from the sea.
He returned to Rome in a grand triumph,
celebrating the day Rome conquered the ocean.
